achieved_rule: reached at least once in 3 (solved_at_least_once); never quotable as a pass rate

container.ships: one arm description, one object description, one container description, and nothing else, on every column
container.why: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T2 grades a physical transfer. Bringing the three bodies into a scene is part of the capability under test, exactly as the conversion is in T1, and this programme is not a cost comparison.
container.no_scene_shipped: No ground, no table, no placement, no launch script, on any column. Where the three bodies go is the agent's decision and a per-simulator starting scene would be a head start for whichever column got one.
container.no_control_shipped: No controller, no trajectory, no inverse-kinematics helper, no grasp pose. The arm is a description with joints, limits and efforts and nothing else.

primitives_only.what: Every link is a box or a cylinder. There is not one mesh in the container and not one external reference.
primitives_only.why: capability-ladder-plan.md section 9 Q4 names the risk that a column fails a tier on a mesh-decoding quirk and the grid reads as a capability verdict. T1's container carries COLLADA meshes and lives with that risk on the record. T2 must not compound it: this tier is decided by COLLISION GEOMETRY -- whether two finger faces can hold a cube -- so a column that cannot decode the visual mesh format would fail for a reason with nothing to do with grasping. The plan's own countermeasure for Q4 is 'a self-contained primitive-geometry description', and this is it.
primitives_only.cost_of_the_choice: The arm is therefore not a robot anybody has ever built, so a column with a first-party model of a REAL arm gets no credit for having it. That is a deliberate trade and it is recorded rather than hidden.
primitives_only.divergence_from_T1_IS_DELIBERATE: DECIDED 2026-08-02, before the freeze, and stated in both task files and in capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 so a reviewer reads a decision rather than an inconsistency. T1 ships a real third-party robot description WITH its COLLADA meshes; T2 ships primitive geometry and not one mesh. Same reasoning, two different tiers: T1 is decided by whether a real robot description can be ingested at all -- that ingestion IS the capability under test there, and the MuJoCo bring-up demonstrated the shipped meshes navigable through that column's own first-party settings (adapters/mujoco/BRINGUP.md) -- while T2 is decided by collision geometry and grasp physics, where a mesh-decoding gap would be a confound with nothing to do with manipulation. Neither choice is the 'safe default' applied twice; each is the choice that keeps its own tier measuring what it says it measures. See tasks/T1_arrive/meta.json container.decided_Q4_T1_SHIPS_THE_MESHES for the other half.

authored_here.what: All three descriptions were authored by the benchmark's own maintainers. None is a vendor model.
authored_here.the_risk: capability-ladder-plan.md section 5a, the trap this whole file exists under: we author the tasks. An arm that no column can use makes the cell a measurement of the asset rather than of the agent, and an arm tuned until OUR column passes is task-rigging. Neither has been ruled out by running anything -- the geometry has been checked for reach (about 0.9 m from a shoulder at z = 0.25) and gripper travel (inner faces 0.078 m apart open, 0.008 m closed, against a 0.05 m cube) and that is ALL that has been checked.
authored_here.before_the_freeze: Demonstrate the transfer once, by hand, on at least one column, and publish the recipe alongside the scaffolding. If it cannot be demonstrated anywhere, the tier is unachievable-as-shipped and that is a finding about this file, not about any simulator.
authored_here.demonstrated: DONE, 2026-08-02, on the MuJoCo column. A scripted (non-agent) oracle assembles the three descriptions into a scene, picks the block off a table, carries it through a 90-degree yaw of the first axis, holds it, lowers it into the bin and lets go -- graded PASS 5/5 through the real ladder.graders.t2 path with NO vacuous clause and NO unanswered channel, hold_mechanism=friction (observed: the model carries zero equality constraints, so the only thing holding the object is contact). Key measurements: lifted clear by up to 0.525 m for a continuous 15.08 s; a 19.42 s run of satisfying 10 s hold windows at 0.0010-0.0057 m RMS in the end-effector's frame; ends at rest (0.00000 m/s over the last 1.0 s) inside the bin with its lowest point 0.020 m against a MEASURED rim of 0.160 m. Two independent cold runs were bit-identical. RE-GRADED 2026-08-02 through the repaired T2.3 (see grading_readings.T2.3_carry_gate) from the same artifacts, no re-simulation: still PASS 5/5, T2.3's window unchanged at a 19.42 s run of satisfying windows, RMS 0.00481 m / max 0.03993 m, 814 of the 1001 samples in the reported window off the surface or moving, and the pre-repair reading ('at rest on a surface throughout') FALSE -- the hold is a real one and it overlaps the 5.48-20.56 s carry T2.2 certifies. RE-GRADED AGAIN 2026-08-02 through the new T2.1 start clause (see grading_readings.T2.1_started_outside_DECIDED_2026-08-02), from the SAME on-disk artifacts, no re-simulation ('--skip-run'): still PASS 5/5, still no vacuous clause and no unanswered channel, hold_mechanism=friction. The new clause is green for a real reason and not by a rounding: the block's centre at the run's first sample is (0.4400, 0.0000, 0.4249) -- on the table -- against a container box spanning x [-0.150, 0.150], y [0.290, 0.590], z [0.000, 0.160], i.e. outside it by 0.29 m in x and 0.29 m in y. Every other measured value in the verdict is byte-identical to the pre-clause grading. One command: python tests/benchmarks/ladder/adapters/mujoco/run_t2.py --out <dir>. Recipe, verbatim verdict, the four things that bite and the effort ledger: tests/benchmarks/ladder/adapters/mujoco/BRINGUP_T2.md. THE TIER IS NOT UNACHIEVABLE-AS-SHIPPED. This says nothing about any agent, and nothing about any other column -- in particular the pre-registered not_achieved expectation for the OmniSim cell below is untouched by it.
what_the_demonstration_found_about_THIS_: WRIST RANGE BINDS BEFORE REACH DOES. The container advertises ~0.9 m of reach, and that is true and is not the constraint. Holding the gripper vertical requires joint_2 + joint_3 + joint_5 = pi, and joint_5 is limited to +/-2.0 rad, so a straight-down grasp needs joint_2 + joint_3 >= 1.14 rad -- the arm must be FOLDED. At the pre-grasp height the oracle uses, radius 0.50 m has no solution while sitting well inside the 0.73 m the two long links span; 0.44 m works. An agent that places the block at 0.6 m and reasons from 'reach is 0.9 m' will fail for a reason it cannot see.

THE FINGER PADS ARE LONGER THAN THE OBJECT. The inner faces span 0.060 m and the cube is 0.050 m, so a centred grasp always puts 5 mm of pad below the object -- into whatever it is standing on. The grasp must be offset upward (the oracle uses 13 mm), which leaves 35 mm of pad-on-block contact.

THE ARM'S SHOULDER OVERLAPS ITS OWN PEDESTAL BY 10 mm (shoulder z in [0.14, 0.26], pedestal z in [0, 0.15]). That is ordinary URDF practice and is harmless wherever a simulator filters parent/child contacts -- but MuJoCo's filter is written over WELD GROUPS and exempts the world body, so ANCHORING the pedestal (which meta.json explicitly permits) makes it collide with the shoulder and jams joint_1 at its full 150 N.m, silently. The free 40 kg pedestal the description intends works; so would an explicit exclude pair.

no_fixed_base_convention.what: The arm has no 'world' link and no fixed joint to one. Its pedestal is 40 kg over a 0.18 m radius instead.
no_fixed_base_convention.why: The world-link idiom is standard ROS practice and is resolved differently by every importer, so shipping it would put a per-simulator convention gap inside a tier about grasping. The pedestal answers the same need with physics every column already has. Anchoring the base is permitted and is not measured.

roles.resolution_rule: The names the descriptions themselves declare. Each of the three is BOTH a robot name and a link name in its own file, so a converter that keys on either produces a body carrying it. The grader prefers the body carrying the declared name and refuses rather than picking the luckiest of several.
roles.why_not_in_the_container: Which body is which is task data. It reaches the agent through the descriptions and the grader through this file; no adapter may supply it, because an adapter that could choose which body counts as 'the object' could choose the one that happens to be in the container.
roles.open_question_for_the_freeze: A converter that renames links (a prefix, a namespace, a de-duplication suffix) produces bodies that carry none of these names, and the grader then refuses the cell rather than grading the wrong body. Whether the roles should also carry an alias list, and who decides an alias is legitimate, is undecided.

harness.why: T2 is graded entirely from the standalone cold re-run. A live session observing the agent's own scene answers nothing T2 asks that the re-run does not answer better -- and a grip that only holds while the agent is watching is exactly what phase B exists to catch.

standalone.note: Phase B, per SPEC 2.3: the deliverable is re-run cold, standalone, with the grader's own sampler injected and no agent present. duration_s must fit the whole motion plus the tier's 10.0 s hold with room to spare; 60 s is roughly three times the shortest plausible attempt.
standalone.surfaces_note: Despite the name, this is the list of non-robot bodies the grader asks the sampler to BOUND at t=0, and T2 needs three kinds of them. (a) Static surfaces: T2.2 measures a lift against them, so a surface nobody bounded is a surface the lift cannot be measured against and the clause reports its witness absent rather than passing. (b) The container: its world-space box is what T2.1's containment test is against, and it is derivable from the t=0 inventory alone -- which is why 'bin' is in this list even though it is not a thing the object rests on. (c) The object: its own bounding box at t=0 is what turns a centre into a lowest point, and without it two of T2.1's clauses grade the centre instead. Names the agent chose differently are simply not bounded; the affected clauses then report their witnesses absent, and the blocker is ours.

constants_note: The first seven are capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T2's own numbers, transcribed. MIN_MASS_KG and MIN_GRAVITY_MPS2 are the tier's 'mass > 0' and 'gravity acting' written as comparable thresholds. MAX_STEP_JUMP_M is now also the tier's own -- T2.4's jump bound was ratified into the plan's table on 2026-08-02 and it is T1.3's number, re-used rather than re-declared (see T2.4_derived_clause). The other three are witness bounds the tier's wording implies rather than states: a jump bound is not a teleport test unless the samples are per-step (MAX_SAMPLE_DT_S), two pose series further apart than MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_S are not one clock and a frame computation across them is meaningless, and a degenerate bounding box is not a container (MIN_CONTAINER_SPAN_M) -- which is also the witness for T2.1's start clause. All are declared here so a reviewer can attack them before the freeze.

hold_mechanism.why_not: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T2, stated so it can be attacked: this tree's own shipped bin-picking success uses a SUCTION end-effector after finger-gripper attempts topped out, and an earlier carry demo used a grasp-stabilisation weld. Failing an attachment-based grasp would be writing the task around a technique we ourselves abandoned -- the inverse of task-rigging and equally uninformative.
hold_mechanism.recorded_where: every verdict's measurements, under 'hold_mechanism', including the verdicts that fail before any physics is read. Section 8 forbids quoting a T2 cell without it.
hold_mechanism.the_cost_of_this_choice: It is a lever we gave ourselves (section 5a admits it). The guard is that the mechanism is printed inside the cell and that no prose may omit it, which is weaker than not having the lever, and is recorded as such.

expectation.omnisim: not_achieved -- expected to FAIL, and said so before running it
expectation.reasoning: capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T2 gives three reasons from this tree: (1) the one-wall pinch of a FREE object was proven not fixable by any parameter here -- sweeps of finger stiffness, contact stiffness, friction, impratio, iterations, commanded width, grasp depth and object mass all failed and the demo was retired; (2) the pinch that does work requires pinning a specific non-default solver, and an agent that does not know to pin it gets a grasp that slips with no error anywhere; (3) the shipped success needed a purpose-built end-effector authored across four documented acts of human iteration. The likely blocker is no_physics_capability (the grip does not hold) or agent_lost (the solver pin is undiscoverable from one sentence).
expectation.if_it_passes: the hold_mechanism field is what tells a reader whether that was a grasp or an attachment.
expectation.pre_registered: capability-ladder-plan.md section 6.4 -- written before any cell runs, printed beside the outcome in the published report.

cost_class: CPU minutes to hours. No GPU required. Training is permitted but not expected.

grading_readings.T2.1_rim: 'The container rim' is not a field any simulator has. The core takes a rim the adapter attests, and otherwise falls back to the top of the container's own bounding box -- the PERMISSIVE reading, which can only make 'below the rim' easier. Which was used is printed in the row, and the fallback marks the clause's witness absent.
grading_readings.T2.1_lowest_point: The pose series carries a centre; the lowest point is that centre minus the object's own vertical half-extent from its t=0 bounding box, which assumes it is not tumbling. For the 0.05 m cube shipped here a fully tumbled pose mis-states the lowest point by up to 0.023 m. With no bounding box at all the CENTRE is graded and the clause reports its witness absent.
grading_readings.T2.2_every_surface: 'Above every static support surface' cannot mean every surface in the world -- an object resting in a bin on the floor is below the top of the table it came from, so the clause could never hold at the end of a successful run. It is read as: at each sample, the clearance to every static bounded surface whose HORIZONTAL FOOTPRINT OVERLAPS the object's, and the smallest of those must be at least LIFT_CLEARANCE_M. Samples with nothing beneath the object are counted and cannot contribute to the window.
grading_readings.T2.3_window: Graded on windows of EXACTLY HOLD_S. The deviation is measured about the window's own mean, so the bound depends on the window and 'the longest window that satisfies it' is not a well-defined maximum. Whether a 10.0 s window exists is decidable, cheap and stable; the longest run of consecutive satisfying windows is reported as a measurement, never as a threshold.
grading_readings.T2.3_carry_gate: DECIDED 2026-08-02, before the freeze, repairing a demonstrated vacuous green (the open question that used to stand here). A window of bounded deviation IN THE END-EFFECTOR'S FRAME is satisfied by two entirely different situations: an object held rigidly, and an object and a carrier that are each independently motionless -- so 'a scene at rest' passed T2.3 outright. The core now requires each candidate window to contain at least one sample at which the object was BEING CARRIED, meaning either (i) clear of everything beneath it by >= LIFT_CLEARANCE_M -- gravity is acting (T2.4 asserts it), so an object off the surface is being held up by something -- or (ii) moving at >= AT_REST_SPEED_MPS -- a moving object that keeps a fixed offset to the carrier is moving WITH it, which is what a grip does. NO THRESHOLD MOVED: 10.0 s / 0.02 m RMS / 0.04 m max are untouched, and both gate numbers are the tier's own (T2.2's clearance and T2.1's definition of at rest). WHY THE DISJUNCTION AND NOT JUST (i), which was the cheapest recorded repair: measured, (i) alone reddens T2.3 on any run that was never lifted, which turns the dragged never_lifted fixture into a two-assertion red, leaves T2.2 with no isolating negative, and makes a 10 s continuous clearance imply T2.2's 3 s one -- i.e. it grades a DRAG, an object genuinely gripped for the whole run, as a failure to grip. That is a tier change smuggled in as a bug fix. (ii) alone fails the most obvious correct answer to 'hold it for ten seconds' -- lift it and stand still -- so neither half is sufficient. The row prints BOTH readings side by side: the graded one, and 'a window inside both bounds in which the object was at rest on a surface throughout', which is exactly what used to be graded as a pass. Negative fixture: at_rest_never_held. Residual limit, stated rather than hidden: the clearance is measured against STATIC surfaces only (T2.2_every_surface), so an object resting motionless on a DYNAMIC body taller than LIFT_CLEARANCE_M reads as airborne -- see T2.2_STATED_LIMIT_resting_on_something_tall, which the owner ratified on 2026-08-02 as a published limit rather than a repair.
grading_readings.T2.3_frame: Measured in the end-effector's frame as the tier states, which needs the carrier's ORIENTATION at every sample on the same clock as the object's. Without it the assertion is red and the frame clause reports itself vacuous -- the core never silently degrades to a world-frame offset, because that reads a rigid hold under rotation as a slip and a slip under no rotation as a hold. The world-frame number is printed beside it, labelled as not being the frame the tier states.
grading_readings.T2.4_derived_clause: STATED AND DECIDED 2026-08-02, before the freeze. It used to read 'the one place this grader goes beyond the plan's text, derived, awaiting the freeze' -- that is no longer true in either direction: the clause is now written into capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T2's own T2.4 row, which states the bound and cites T1.3's constant, so the plan and the core say the same thing and neither is deriving anything from the other. WHAT IT IS: T2 as written had no teleport guard -- mass, dynamic and gravity catch a kinematic prop but NOT a scripted position write onto a body that genuinely has mass. The tier's own gloss on T2.4 is 'a kinematic prop being flown to the bin fails here', and a body that jumps 0.5 m between physics steps is being flown as surely as a massless one is. So T2.4 carries a fourth clause reusing T1.3's own MAX_STEP_JUMP_M and its MAX_SAMPLE_DT_S rate witness -- no new number is declared anywhere, and a series too coarse to see a jump makes the clause report its witness absent rather than passing it. Negative fixture: teleported_object (one 0.9 m inter-sample jump mid-carry, with the tool jumping too, so the frame-relative hold check still reads it as a rigid grip -- which is exactly the artifact only a motion-plausibility clause can catch).
grading_readings.T2.5: As T1.5. A missing engine attribution makes the cell INVALID, not FAIL -- an unattributed physics result is not a result.
grading_readings.T2.3_REPAIRED_2026-08-02: THE DEFECT, KEPT ON THE RECORD NOW THAT IT IS FIXED. As written, T2.3 was satisfied by 'everything stopped': it asked whether SOME continuous HOLD_S window exists in which the object's position in the end-effector's frame varies by <= HOLD_RMS_M RMS, and nothing required anything to be happening in that window. Demonstrated numerically on the achievability run's own final state -- block resting on the bin floor, jaws open, arm parked 0.6 m away, nothing in contact -- a 12 s window scored RMS 4.0e-08 m and max excursion 3.8e-15 m and PASSED. Nothing was held. The scripted oracle never exploited it (its final settle is 4.0 s, so the only 10 s window in its run is the carry), but a cell that ended with a long quiet tail would have satisfied the clause without ever gripping anything. Same class as the A1.3 (id,id) contact bug that sat green for weeks. Found by the MuJoCo achievability proof, 2026-08-02 (ladder/adapters/mujoco/BRINGUP_T2.md section 5); repaired the same day -- see T2.3_carry_gate for the repair and the argument for the reading chosen over the two alternatives. Regression: the at_rest_never_held negative fixture, which is a genuine transfer whose jaws were only closed 7.0 s and whose ten still seconds are the parked tail afterwards. The MuJoCo oracle re-grades PASS 5/5 through the repaired grader with an unchanged 19.42 s run of satisfying windows, 814 of the 1001 samples in the reported window off the surface or moving, and 'at rest on a surface throughout' FALSE.
grading_readings.T2.2_STATED_LIMIT_resting_on_something_t: A STATED LIMIT AT THE FREEZE (ratified 2026-08-02), DEMONSTRATED, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED -- it used to stand here as an open question and the owner has now decided it stays as a published limit rather than a repair. WHY NOT FIXED: closing it needs the world AABB of every DYNAMIC body at every sample, which no column in the roster supplies today; a clause written against evidence nobody has is a clause whose witness is permanently absent, which is precisely the vacuity this tier's pre-freeze audit spent itself eliminating (see T2.3_REPAIRED_2026-08-02). Writing it into the plan's T2 text as a known limit, with its containment, is the honest alternative and is what was done. THE LIMIT ITSELF: 'Lifted clear' is satisfiable by an object that never moved. T2.2_every_surface reads the clause against STATIC bounded surfaces only (a body that can move is not a fixed datum), so an object resting motionless on a DYNAMIC body -- a crate, a pallet, another block -- has its clearance measured to the static floor UNDER that body. Demonstrated: a block at rest for a whole 20 s run on a 0.10 m dynamic crate scores 'longest continuous window clear by >= 0.05 m: 20.0 s' and T2.2 reads GREEN, and after the 2026-08-02 repair T2.3 inherits it (the same samples read as airborne). What contains it today: the object's centre must still end inside the container's AABB below its rim (T2.1), and on the container this task ships a crate tall enough to clear the bin's own 0.16 m rim by LIFT_CLEARANCE_M would put the block's centre above the bin's box, so the FULL cell does not pass on this hole -- T2.1 was red in the demonstration. Fixing it needs evidence no column supplies today (the world AABB of every DYNAMIC body at every sample, not just the static ones at t=0). The containment above is what makes it publishable as a limit rather than a hole: it is stated in capability-ladder-plan.md section 2 T2, it is stated here, and no T2 cell may be quoted without it being available to the reader.
grading_readings.T2.1_started_outside_DECIDED_2026-08-02: DECIDED AND FIXED before the freeze, by the owner, on a demonstrated defect. THE DEFECT: T2 graded an END STATE (T2.1), a LIFT (T2.2) and a HOLD (T2.3), and not one of the five assertions read where the object began -- so a run that picks the block OUT of the bin, holds it 12 s in the air over the bin and puts it back graded PASS 5/5. Demonstrated on the synthetic fixture scene: T2.1 green (ends inside, under the rim, at rest), T2.2 green (clear for far longer than the 3 s asked), T2.3 green (a genuine rigid carry through a 90-degree yaw), T2.4 and T2.5 green. No transfer happened. The tier's OUTCOME sentence says 'an object that STARTS ON A SURFACE ends up inside a container', so this was the tier failing to grade what it states, and only the graded rows were silent. THE FIX: T2.1 carries a fourth clause -- the object's centre at the run's FIRST SAMPLE must be OUTSIDE the container's AABB. It is measured on the same series, same body and same clock as the 'ends inside' clause it mirrors (the first sample of exactly the series whose last sample was already graded), so any column that can answer one answers the other by construction and NO NEW CHANNEL IS REQUIRED; the t=0 inventory carries the same fact independently. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASSERT: 'on a surface'. That would grade where the agent chose to set the object down before starting, which is scene authorship, not transfer. Witness: the same non-degenerate container box the containment clause needs -- with no usable box, 'outside it' is not a measurement and the clause reports itself vacuous rather than passing. Negative fixture: started_in_the_container, which reddens T2.1 and NO OTHER assertion, and within T2.1 reddens ONLY the new clause (inside / under the rim / at rest all stay green). Re-graded from the MuJoCo achievability run's own on-disk artifacts, no re-simulation: still PASS 5/5, with the block starting at (0.440, 0.000, 0.425) against a container box spanning x [-0.150, 0.150], y [0.290, 0.590], z [0.000, 0.160] -- outside it by 0.29 m in x, so the oracle passes the new clause for a real reason and not by a rounding.
grading_readings.T1_SIBLING_AUDIT_2026-08-02: The same sweep, run over T1 while T2.3 was being repaired. TWO findings, both DEMONSTRATED on deliberately wrong artifacts, in both of which the grader implements the tier's own wording faithfully and the gap is in what that wording can see. Dispositions, ruled by the owner 2026-08-02 before the freeze: (1) recorded, contained, not changed; (2) RESOLVED by relabelling the row, with the stronger reading declined on the record. (1) T1.4's during-motion half is WAIVED when no contact carries a timestamp ('ok = bool(support) and (bool(hits) if timed else True)'), so a robot that NEVER MOVED passes T1.4 on untimed contacts -- demonstrated, T1.4 green with the 'touched it while moving' clause reporting its witness absent, which is the disclosure the ladder's vacuity machinery exists for and is already dogfooded by the untimed_contacts fixture. It is contained: such a run fails T1.1/T1.3 on the pose series, and the frozen bundle's own contact channel is sampled before the settle phase, which ladder_evidence gap 2 already states. Making it a hard FAIL would turn a scaffolding gap into somebody else's product failure, which section 4 forbids. (2) RESOLVED 2026-08-02 by relabelling, not by re-checking -- see tasks/T1_arrive/meta.json grading_readings.T1.4_LABEL_FIXED_2026-08-02 and .T1.4_stronger_reading_CONSIDERED_AND_DECLINED. The finding stands as recorded: T1.4 was labelled 'under its own actuation' and MEASURES 'a contact naming the robot and a distinct non-robot body, seen while the robot was moving' -- which a robot riding a moving pallet or conveyor satisfies, demonstrated by T1 grading PASS 5/5 on a robot whose only support contact is with a body named 'pallet'. The owner's decision was to fix the LABEL and leave the CHECK alone: the row is now 'touched the surface while moving' in t1_core, in T1's meta.json and in the plan's own T1 table, and the stronger reading (detect actuation) is recorded as considered and DECLINED because no column in the roster supplies wheel torque, motor command or joint velocity, so the clause would redden cells for a channel WE never built. Not one measured value changed.

negative_fixtures.rule: capability-ladder-plan.md section 5c.2: no assertion enters a ladder cell until it has been observed FAILING on a deliberately wrong artifact. Each fixture is the oracle with ONE thing wrong and must redden its own assertion AND NO OTHER -- a null agent turning everything red does not satisfy the rule.
